references.text: According to the Mosaic Law, it was the priests who were to examine and declare a leper clean. Jesus refers to this regulation by sending the lepers to the priests ([ref:3 Mos 13:49|Leviticus 13:49]).
The law prescribed a detailed cleansing procedure for lepers who had been healed. The priests were to inspect them and carry out the cleansing ritual ([ref:3 Mos 14:2-4|Leviticus 14:2-4]).
The offering that the cleansed leper was to bring to the priest is described here. Jesus sends the ten there precisely to fulfill this legal requirement ([ref:3 Mos 14:10-11|Leviticus 14:10-11]).

Na'aman was instructed by the prophet Elisha to wash in the Jordan River to be cleansed of his leprosy. There too, the healing occurred on the way as he obeyed in faith—a clear parallel theme to the ten lepers who were cleansed while they went ([ref:2 Kong 5:10-14|2 Kings 5:10-14]).
Also after healing a leper, Jesus commanded him to go and show himself to the priest and offer the sacrifice that Moses had required, as a testimony ([ref:Matt 8:4|Matthew 8:4]).
Mark recounts the same practice: Jesus sends the healed leper to the priest to show himself and offer what Moses prescribed ([ref:Mark 1:44|Mark 1:44]).
Earlier in Luke's Gospel, Jesus also sent a leper to the priest after healing him, with the command to offer the sacrifice that Moses had ordained ([ref:Luk 5:14|Luke 5:14]).

After the healing on the way, Jesus said to the one who returned, "Your faith has saved you." This shows that the faith which caused them to go before they were healed was decisive ([ref:Luk 17:19|Luke 17:19]).

Also the royal official believed Jesus' words and went—and discovered on the way that the healing had taken place. The same pattern of faith and healing on the way is found here ([ref:Joh 4:50-52|John 4:50-52]).

The Letter to the Hebrews describes how Abraham, in faith, obeyed and went out without knowing where he was going. The lepers showed similar faith by going to the priests before they were yet healed ([ref:Hebr 11:8|Hebrews 11:8]).
